decisions.quote: This study re-estimated their main model specifications by attempting to re-construct their data. I also extended the data sample to a more recent period (1996 to 2015).
decisions.reason: The original authors no longer had their dataset, so the author newly collected/reconstructed the 1970-1996 data from OECD databases and library books and also collected a new sample covering 1996-2015 to re-test the original findings. Under the codebook, re-testing a published finding using newly collected data and a new sample Period (1996-2015) is a replication.

decisions.quote: My replication confirmed their finding that merit goods and private consumption are complements. On the other hand, I did not find support for their conclusion that public goods and private consumption are substitutes.
decisions.reason: Although the author states in the results section that the empirical point estimates are similar to the original study's, the paper explicitly frames its substantive conclusion in the abstract, results, and conclusion as confirming the original finding of complementarity between merit goods and private consumption while finding no support for the original conclusion of substitutability between public goods and private consumption. Under the codebook, when the authors frame their evidence as confirming one main tested finding but not supporting the other, the outcome is mixed.
